G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.2, printed pages 175-177 (PDF pages 187-189): the one-parameter unitary groups of rotations, their generators and the commutation relations on the Schwartz class

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Sections 1.1-1.2, printed pages 1-9 (PDF pages 1-9): definition of the angular momentum operators and their commutation relations

items.title: The free flow as a unimodular multiplier in the momentum representation
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, a mass parameter $m>0$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U^{(r)}$ be
the momentum unitary of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], and
let
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
which is self-adjoint with the displayed domain
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)). Write
$M_{a}$ for multiplication by a measurable function $a$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ and put $f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$
([[def-complex-exponential]]). Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}H_{0}U^{(r)-1}=M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)}$ as self-adjoint operators, with
domain $D(M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)})=\{g\in L^{2}:\ |p|^{2}g\in L^{2}\}$;

(b) $U^{(r)}\,e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}}$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $\psi\in H^{(r)}$, every $t$ and almost every $p$,
$$\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)=f_{t}(p)\,\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p),\qquad \bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|=\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|;$$
consequently the spectral outcome law of each $P_{k}$ is independent of $t$;
and $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ for every $t$, where
$\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; integers
$r\ge1$; $m,\hbar>0$; the space $H^{(r)}$; the componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$; the momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$; the free operator $H_{0}$; a
vector $\psi\in H^{(r)}$; a Schwartz class $u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$; real $t$.

[F1] **Free operator.** $H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ is self-adjoint; it is the componentwise
assembly of the scalar free operators of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), which are self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$
per component and equal $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta$ on Schwartz classes
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (b),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a), [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

[F2] **Momentum representation.** $U^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$ with $U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)}$, and
$U^{(r)}$ maps $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ onto itself and acts there by the
componentwise Fourier transform with normalization $(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (b),
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]).

[F3] **Domain in momentum form.** With $p$ the momentum variable of [F2],
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=\{\psi\in H^{(r)}:\ |p|^{2}U^{(r)}\psi\in L^{2}\}$
and
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=\{\psi:p_{k}U^{(r)}\psi\in L^{2}\ \forall k\}$
as sets, by the Fourier characterization of integer-order Sobolev spaces read in the normalization of [F2]
([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]],
[[thm-plancherel]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

[F4] **Conjugation calculus.** For a unitary $W$ and a self-adjoint $K$ with
spectral PVM $E_K$, the operator $WKW^{-1}$ with domain $WD(K)$ is self-adjoint
with PVM $WE_K(\cdot)W^{-1}$ and flow $e^{-itWKW^{-1}/\hbar}=We^{-itK/\hbar}W^{-1}$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]] clause (a)),
and if two self-adjoint operators have a common domain $D$ and agree on a dense
linear subspace of $D$, then they are equal: their difference is symmetric on
$D$ and vanishes on a dense subspace, hence is zero
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

[F5] **Multiplier spectral data.** For a real measurable finite-valued function
$a$ the multiplication operator $M_{a}$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is self-adjoint with domain $\{g:ag\in L^{2}\}$ and spectral PVM
$M_{\mathbf 1_{a^{-1}(B)}}$; for bounded Borel $h$ the bounded calculus satisfies
$\Phi_{M_a}(h)=M_{h\circ a}$ and $\|M_{g}\|=\sup|g|$; these are the componentwise
versions of the scalar multiplier facts
([[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]],
[[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

[F6] **Density.** $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ is dense in $H^{(r)}$
([[lem-schwartz-space-is-dense-in-l-two]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the momentum-space form of the free
operator as a multiplier, obtain the flow by the conjugation calculus and read
the modulus invariance and Schwartz preservation off the multiplier formula.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Momentum form of the free operator] Put $M:=M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)}$, self-adjoint with domain $D(M)=U^{(r)}W^{2,2}$ by [F3] and [F5], and put $A:=U^{(r)-1}MU^{(r)}=U^{(r)*}MU^{(r)}$; by [F4] $A$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=U^{(r)-1}D(M)=W^{2,2}$. On a Schwartz class $u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ one has $P_{k}^{2}u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ by [F2] and hence $H_{0}u=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}u$ by [F1], while $U^{(r)}H_{0}u=M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)}U^{(r)}u$ by [F2]; thus $Au=H_{0}u$ for every $u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$. Both operators are self-adjoint with the common domain $W^{2,2}$ and agree on the dense subspace $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ [F6], so $A=H_{0}$ by [F4], which is (a). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 [Flow] Applying the flow identity of [F4] to $A=U^{(r)-1}MU^{(r)}=H_{0}$ gives $U^{(r)-1}\,e^{-itM/\hbar}\,U^{(r)}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, hence by the functional calculus of [F5] $M_{f_{t}}=e^{-itM/\hbar}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, and therefore $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}}$, which is (b). [step 1.1, F4, F5, given, algebra]

3.1 [Pointwise phase and modulus] Writing $g:=U^{(r)}\psi$, step 2.1 gives $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi=M_{f_{t}}g$ with $|f_{t}(p)|=1$ for every $p$, so the two displays of (c) hold for almost every $p$. [step 2.1, F2, given, algebra]

3.2 [Schwartz preservation] Let $u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$; by [F2], $g:=U^{(r)}u\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$. The function $p\mapsto f_{t}(p)g(p)$ is smooth, and every seminorm $\sup_{p}|p^{\alpha}\partial^{\beta}(f_{t}g)(p)|$ is finite because $f_{t}$ is a unimodular exponential of a polynomial and hence has derivatives of polynomial growth while $g$ is Schwartz; thus $f_{t}g\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$, and $U^{(r)-1}(f_{t}g)\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ by [F2] again. Applying the same argument to $-t$ gives the reverse inclusion, so $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$. [step 2.1, F2, F5, given, algebra]

4.1 [Momentum laws] By [F2], $E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(r)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_B(p_{k})}U^{(r)}$, so for a unit $\psi$ the law is $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\|M_{\mathbf 1_B(p_{k})}U^{(r)}\psi\|^{2}=\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}|(U^{(r)}\psi)(p)|^{2}dp$; by step 3.1 the modulus $|(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi)(p)|$ equals $|(U^{(r)}\psi)(p)|$ almost everywhere, so the integral is independent of $t$. [step 3.1, F2, F5, given, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b), and steps 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 prove (c): the pointwise phase and modulus, the Schwartz invariance and the momentum laws. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is not claimed.** No free propagator integral kernel, no pointwise
  trajectory of the particle, and no assertion that the momentum representative's
  modulus is measurable-free (it is an $L^{2}$ class; the invariance is that of
  the class of the modulus) appear in this lemma.
- **Scope.** The statement is purely mathematical, about the free operator on
  $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$; the physical reading of the momentum
  laws is that of the observable and probability postulate.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 7.3, printed pages 169-171 (PDF pages 181-183): the time evolution in the free case as multiplication by a unimodular function of the momentum variable, with the Fourier transform

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.3 and 3.3, printed pages 15-25 (PDF pages 15-25): the free evolution operator in momentum space and its action as a phase multiplication

items.title: Symmetries of the declared dynamics, unitary symmetry groups and conserved sharp observables
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
examples of candidate symmetry groups, whose actual symmetry property for a
given dynamics is a theorem of this page, are:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. the **gauge multipliers** $G_{\chi}$ of the prescribed-coupling model of
   this page, whose definition and covariance statements are given on the
   gauge items of this page.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$, $\Pi$ or $G_{\chi}$ is a symmetry of a given
bounded-potential or prescribed-coupling dynamics is a conditional theorem of
this page. Antiunitary symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of
preparations as opposed to dynamics, and any empirical claim about which
symmetries a laboratory system possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].

## Remarks

- **Why the energy domain appears.** For an unbounded energy operator, the
  statement "$S$ commutes with $H_{\mathrm{op}}$" needs the domain equality
  $SD(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ to make the operator identity
  meaningful; this is the same convention under which the covariance theorems
  of the kinematics page are stated.
- **Candidate actions are not symmetries by definition.** The translations,
  rotations, parity and gauge multipliers are defined as unitaries or unitary
  families; the definition records them as the model's candidate symmetry
  actions, and the theorems decide for which potentials or couplings each
  candidate is actually a symmetry.
items.physical_scope: The symmetry and conservation vocabulary of the declared framework model: symmetries of the dynamics of a declared isolated system as unitaries preserving the energy domain and commuting with the energy operator, unitary symmetry groups and their strong continuity, one-parameter symmetry groups and their Stone generators, and the reading of a conserved sharp observable as one whose outcome law is time-independent in every preparation. The item fixes terminology and candidate actions of the model (translations, spatial rotations, parity, and the gauge multipliers defined on the gauge page); it asserts no symmetry of any concrete model potential or external coupling, no antiunitary or superselection structure, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1-4.3, printed pages 58-70 (PDF pages 66-78): unitary transformation operators, generators of continuous transformations, symmetries and conservation laws

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pages 18-22 (PDF pages 18-22): Heisenberg operators, conserved operators commuting with the Hamiltonian and their constant time dependence

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.2 printed pages 115-117 (PDF pages 127-129) and Theorem 8.1 printed page 174 (PDF page 186): commuting self-adjoint operators and the Noether-type conservation statement

items.title: Prescribed external electromagnetic coupling P5a: the minimal-coupling model and its gauge transformations
items.statement:
## Postulate

Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, additional to P1-P5 and valid
only for the model of this page, the following prescribed-coupling statement
for a **spinless** particle. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice
hypotheses of the cited magnetic-operator suppliers.

**(i) Frame and particle data.** Fix a named Newtonian inertial frame in the
class of P5 and a declared spinless particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and charge
parameter $q\in\mathbb R$; the model state space is the scalar component of the
massive model, $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, with the position and momentum
operators of the massive model. The frame, the mass and the charge are part of
the model specification; the frame is not derived from the potentials, and
$m$ and $q$ are empirical parameters of a species when one is identified.

**(ii) Admissible prescribed potentials.** The external data are an
**admissible pair** $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]: real
classes $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}=(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ with
$A_{j}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$ whose weak first derivatives
$D_{k}A_{j}$ are bounded, and $\Phi_{\rm ext}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). The potentials are **prescribed**: no
field equation, source model or back-reaction is assumed.

**(iii) Energy operator.** The model's energy operator is the
minimal-coupling magnetic Schrodinger operator
$$H_{\rm ext}:=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}},\qquad D(H_{\rm ext})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]], that is
$$H_{\rm ext}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(P_{j}-qA_{{\rm ext},j}(Q)\bigr)^{2}+q\,\Phi_{\rm ext}(Q)$$
on the displayed domain. This operator is self-adjoint with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]], so
it satisfies the self-adjointness requirement of the dynamics postulate P4 in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; the
adoption here is the identification of this operator as the energy of the
declared particle, which is a model assumption and not a consequence of
P1-P5.

**(iv) Units.** Use the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]];
the additional assignments are: $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ in
$\mathrm{T\,m}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$, $\Phi_{\rm ext}$ in V, $q$ in C, so
$q\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ has momentum units and $q\Phi_{\rm ext}$ energy units.
The exponential of clause (vi) uses [[def-complex-exponential]] and
$\chi$ is measured in $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, so the phase $q\chi/\hbar$ is
dimensionless.

**(v) Field definitions.** Define, wherever the displayed derivatives exist as
weak derivatives, $\mathbf B:=\nabla\times\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ in T and
$\mathbf E:=-\nabla\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. These are **definitions of the model's field symbols**;
they assert no Maxwell equation, no relation to measured fields, and no
coupling of the particle back on the sources.

**(vi) Gauge transformations.** For a real gauge function $\chi$ in the
regularity class of the gauge items of this page, the model relates the pair
$(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ to
$$\mathbf A'_{\rm ext}=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\qquad \Phi'_{\rm ext}=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi,$$
and the state phase by $\psi'=e^{iq\chi/\hbar}\psi$. The operator consequences,
the criterion under which the multiplier is a symmetry of a fixed model, and
the propagator transported to the transformed pair are proved on this page for
the stated regularity; the **reading** that the two coefficient pairs describe
the same physical situation is part of this assumption, not a theorem, and the
theorem statements of this page are independent of that reading.

**(vii) Status and scope.** Clauses (i)-(vi) are adopted model assumptions for
the declared potential class only. They assert nothing about a laboratory
realization, about field sources, about singular or unbounded potentials,
about time-dependent data beyond the hypotheses of the gauge items, about
statistical or measurement models, or about the accuracy of the spinless
minimal-coupling description of any species; the identification of a physical
arrangement with the model is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

## Status and scope

- **What is assumed and what is proved.** The minimal-coupling form of the
  energy operator, the field definitions and the gauge transformation formulas
  are adopted; self-adjointness on $W^{2,2}$ is a mathematical theorem cited
  from the magnetic-operator development, and the covariance, symmetry and
  propagator consequences are proved on this page.
- **Bounded coefficients only.** The assumption is restricted to admissible
  pairs with bounded potentials and bounded weak first derivatives; Coulomb,
  singular, unbounded and general time-dependent potentials are separate model
  realizations requiring their own self-adjointness and evolution statements.
- **No Maxwell theory.** The field symbols of clause (v) are definitions; no
  Maxwell equation, constitutive relation or measured field value appears.
items.physical_scope: The prescribed-external-coupling assumption P5a of the framework: a spinless particle of mass m>0 and charge q in a named Newtonian inertial frame with admissible prescribed potentials (A,Phi) of the bounded-coefficient class, whose energy operator is the minimal-coupling magnetic Schrodinger operator on the domain W^{2,2}; the adopted field definitions, the units, and the adopted gauge transformation of potentials and state phase. Adoption is a model assumption for the stated potential class; it asserts no Maxwell equation or source model, no time-dependent well-posedness beyond the stated class, no derivation from P1-P5, and no identification of any laboratory arrangement or measured field with the declared data.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 3.3 and its subsection 'Gauge transformations', printed pages 45-47 (PDF pages 53-55): the Hamiltonian (3.31) of a charged particle in a magnetic field with minimal coupling, and the gauge transformation of the potentials and of the phase of the wave function (equations (3.43)-(3.45)); PDF page = printed page + 8

J. Zinn-Justin and R. Guida, 'Gauge invariance', Scholarpedia 3(12):8287 (2008), Section 2.2 'Quantum Hamiltonian in a magnetic field and gauge invariance', equations (15)-(18): the unitary transformation U=exp(i e Omega(q)/hbar) transporting the covariant momentum and the Hamiltonian to the gauge-transformed vector potential, and the corresponding transformation of the state phase (their sign convention is A^Omega = A - grad Omega with charge e)

items.title: Conservation of a symmetry generator: commuting flows, energy compatibility and conserved outcome laws
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a declared isolated
system with state space $H$, assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$
and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); use the symmetry vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]. Assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the
system with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and put
$W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

(ii) $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(iii) $U(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$.

When they hold:

(a) **Conserved law.** The outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is time-independent: for
every preparation $\rho$, every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)\ \text{for a unit }\psi\ \text{with }\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0).$$

(b) **Conserved moments.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector, then the mean and
the second moment of the law of $A$ in the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are
finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; if a moment is infinite at
$t=0$, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(c) **Unitary symmetries of the dynamics.** If a unitary operator $S$ is a
symmetry in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]], that is
$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and
$S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, then $S\,U(t)=U(t)\,S$ for every $t$;
if in addition $S$ is self-adjoint, then the outcome law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S,u_S)$ with its spectral coordinate unit is time-independent in
every preparation.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2 and P4
and the cited mathematics. Its symmetry hypothesis is the strong commutation of
the flows or, equivalently, of the spectral measures, not a formal commutator
identity on a small domain; no definite value of a conserved observable is
asserted; no converse from the constancy of laws to the commutation conditions
is claimed for unbounded $A$; and no concrete model potential, apparatus,
measurement record or empirical result is introduced.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4 in the stated readings; the Axioms of
Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the assigned energy observable
$(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$, its PVM $E_H$ and flow $U(t)$; an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_A)$ with PVM $E_A$ and group $W(s)$; a unitary $S$ and a
self-adjoint unitary $S$ in clause (c); a preparation $\rho$; a unit vector
$\psi$; a Borel set $B$; real $s,t$.

[F1] **Model readings.** $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $A$ are densely defined
self-adjoint operators with regular spectral PVMs $E_H,E_A$ and flows
$U(t)=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar}$, $W(s)=e^{-isA/\hbar}$; $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$
and $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi$ are the preparation evolutions of P4
([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a)-(c),
[[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a),(d),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b),
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]],
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

[F2] **Conjugation and commutation calculus.** For self-adjoint $K,A$ with
flows $U_K,U_A$ the conditions (i), (ii), (iii) of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]] clause (b)
are equivalent; under them $E_A(B)U_K(t)=U_K(t)E_A(B)$ for all $B,t$ (clause
(d)); and for a unitary $W$ one has $E_{WKW^{*}}(B)=WE_K(B)W^{*}$ and
$e^{-itWKW^{*}/\hbar}=We^{-itK/\hbar}W^{*}$ (clause (a)).

[F3] **Conserved spectral laws.** If a PVM $F$ commutes with $E_H$ in the
strong spectral sense, then $\operatorname{tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}F(S))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$
for every density operator $\rho$ and every $S$, and
$\|F(S)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|F(S)\psi\|^{2}$ for every unit $\psi$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]]
clause (b)).

[F4] **Outcome laws and moments.** $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$
and $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$; for a unit $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean
and second moment of the law exist and equal $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|A\psi\|^{2}$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b),(e),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]]).

[F5] **Energies and unitaries.** A self-adjoint unitary $S$ has spectral PVM
supported on $\{-1,1\}$ and its own flow $e^{-isS/\hbar}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; translate the model data into the mathematical
conjugation calculus, transfer the conservation theorem for commuting spectral
families, and handle the discrete unitary symmetry by the generator comparison.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Translation of the model data] By [F1] the operators $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $A$ are self-adjoint on the Hilbert space $H$ of the declared system, with flows $U$ and $W$ exactly as in [F2]; hence the equivalence of (i), (ii) and (iii) below is the equivalence stated in [F2] for the pair $K:=H_{\mathrm{op}}$, $A$: condition (i) is the commutation of the two flows, condition (ii) the strong commutation of $E_H$ and $E_A$, and condition (iii) the domain invariance and conjugation identity for $A$ under $U$. This proves the equivalence. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 [Conserved law] Assume (ii), so that $F:=E_A$ commutes with $E_H$ in the strong spectral sense. Applying [F3] with $S:=B$ to the preparation $\rho$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}E_A(B))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$, and by [F4] this is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B)$. The pure form follows from the second display of [F3] with the unit vector $\psi(0)$ and [F4]. This proves (a). [step 1.1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.2 [Unitary symmetries commute with the flow] Let $S$ be unitary with $S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, that is $SH_{\mathrm{op}}S^{*}=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with domain $SD(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$. By [F2] applied with $W:=S$ and $K:=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ one has $e^{-itSH_{\mathrm{op}}S^{*}/\hbar}=Se^{-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar}S^{*}$ for every $t$; the left-hand operator is $e^{-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar}=U(t)$ and the right-hand one is $SU(t)S^{*}$, so $SU(t)S^{*}=U(t)$ and, multiplying on the right by $S$, $SU(t)=U(t)S$. [step 1.1, F2, given, algebra]

3.1 [Conserved moments] Let $\psi\in D(A)$ be a unit vector. By [F4] the mean and second moment of the law of $A$ in $[\psi(0)]$ exist and equal $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; since by step 2.1 the law itself is the same measure at every time, its moments are the same extended real numbers at every time, hence finite and time-independent with the displayed values. If the second moment is infinite at $t=0$, [F4] does not apply and no equality is claimed. This proves (b). [step 2.1, F4, given, algebra]

3.2 [Self-adjoint symmetries have conserved laws] Let $S$ be unitary and self-adjoint with $SH_{\mathrm{op}}S^{*}=H_{\mathrm{op}}$. By step 2.2, $SU(t)=U(t)S$; multiplying on the left by $U(t)^{*}$ gives $U(t)^{*}SU(t)=S$, and conjugating this identity by the unitary $U(t)$ gives $U(t)SU(t)^{*}=S$ as well. Apply the flow identity of [F2] with $W:=U(t)^{*}$ and $K:=S$, at time parameter $s$: $e^{-isU(t)^{*}SU(t)/\hbar}=U(t)^{*}e^{-isS/\hbar}U(t)$; since $U(t)^{*}SU(t)=S$, the left side is $e^{-isS/\hbar}$, so $U(t)$ commutes with $e^{-isS/\hbar}$ for every $s$. Writing $W_{S}(s):=e^{-isS/\hbar}$, this says $W_{S}(s)U(t)=U(t)W_{S}(s)$ for all $s,t$, which is condition (i) for the pair $(S,H_{\mathrm{op}})$; by the equivalence of step 1.1 condition (ii) holds for that pair, and applying step 2.1 to the self-adjoint operator $S$ gives the time-independence of the law of $(S,u_S)$ in every preparation. This proves (c). [step 2.2, step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F5, given, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves the equivalence, steps 2.1 and 3.1 prove (a) and (b), step 2.2 proves the first part of (c) and step 3.2 its second part; clause (d) records the hypotheses actually used (P1, P2, P4, strong commutation of flows or spectral measures) and the exclusions (no definite value, no unbounded converse, no concrete model or empirical claim). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, step 3.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Energy conservation is the special case $A=H_{\mathrm{op}}$.** With $A=H_{\mathrm{op}}$ the conditions (i)-(iii) hold trivially, and clause (a) reproduces the conservation of the energy law proved on the autonomous-dynamics page; the content here is the transfer to any other generator.
- **Commutation on a small domain is excluded.** The equivalence proved is between the flow commutation (i) and the strong spectral commutation (ii); a formal identity $[A,H_{\mathrm{op}}]\psi=0$ on a small domain is neither a hypothesis nor a conclusion.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state, observable and autonomous-dynamics postulates P1, P2 and P4 for a declared isolated system: for a self-adjoint assigned sharp observable A whose one-parameter unitary group commutes with the flow, the three formulations (commuting flows, strong commutation of the spectral measures, and invariance of the domain of A under the flow with U(t)*AU(t)=A) are equivalent, the outcome law of A is time-independent in every preparation, its mean and second moment are conserved whenever they exist, and a unitary symmetry of the dynamics commutes with the flow, its being self-adjoint making its own outcome law time-independent. The statement asserts no symmetry of any concrete model, no definite value of a conserved observable, no apparatus realization, no equilibration statement and no empirical result, and uses the strong-commutation hypothesis rather than a formal commutator on a small domain.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 4.2, printed pages 115-117 (PDF pages 127-129): commuting self-adjoint operators, Lemma 4.5 and the equivalence with commutation of the one-parameter groups; Theorem 8.1, printed page 174 (PDF page 186): invariant domain and conserved expectations

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): the Heisenberg equation, operators commuting with the Hamiltonian and constant Heisenberg representatives

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.3-4.4, printed pages 68-71 (PDF pages 76-79): commuting observables, invariance under displacements, conserved quantities and the Heisenberg picture

items.title: Translation invariance of bounded potentials and conservation of momentum
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]),
let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1}),\qquad V_{a}(x):=V(x-a),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with $M_{V}$ multiplication by
$V$ and $T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(2s+1)}$ the componentwise translations
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]]). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$:
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},$$
and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $T_{a}$ is a symmetry for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, then $V$ is almost
everywhere constant; in that case $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$ for
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and $c$ the constant, and the translations
form a strongly continuous unitary group of symmetries;

(c) **Momentum conservation for translation-invariant models.** Let $V$ be
almost everywhere constant and let $c$ be that constant. Then for every
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is a conserved observable of the
model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
if $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ is a unit vector, the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are conserved with time-zero values $\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; and the coordinate translations satisfy
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ for all $t$, so the generators of the
one-parameter symmetry groups are the momentum components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. It asserts no momentum conservation for a
potential that is not translation invariant — the translation-covariance
theorem transports the position law and conjugates the dynamics, but does not
by itself conserve momentum — and it makes no claim about singular, unbounded,
periodic, boundary or relativistic models, no discrete symmetry group, no
apparatus and no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the Axioms
of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space $H_{s}$; the
operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$; a real bounded measurable $V$;
the operator $H_{V}$; a preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set
$B$; $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$; $k\in\{1,2,3\}$; $t\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Translations and the bounded-potential operator.** $T_{a}$ is unitary
with $T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I$,
$T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, $T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, and
$T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$; $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$; and
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ with the generator identification of the
translation group ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] clause (c),
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (c),(d)).

[F2] **Multipliers.** $M_{V}$ is the bounded self-adjoint multiplication
operator by the real bounded class $V$; for two real bounded measurable
functions $W_{1},W_{2}$ one has $M_{W_{1}}=M_{W_{2}}$ if and only if
$W_{1}=W_{2}$ almost everywhere; and $H_{V}=H_{0}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint with
domain $W^{2,2}$ and generates a strongly continuous unitary group
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F3] **Mollifiers and Lebesgue points.** Let $\rho$ be a unit-mass radial
mollifier with support in $B_{1}(0)$ and $\rho_{\varepsilon}(x)=\varepsilon^{-3}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$
its family ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]],
[[def-radial-mollifier-family-in-rn]]). For $f\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and a
Lebesgue point $x$ of $f$ one has $(f*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x)\to f(x)$ as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$
([[lem-radial-majorized-kernels-recover-lebesgue-point-values]],
[[def-lebesgue-point-and-lebesgue-set]]); almost every point is a Lebesgue
point of $f$ ([[thm-almost-every-point-is-a-lebesgue-point]]); and for a
bounded measurable $V$ the products $V\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-\cdot)$ are
integrable and dominated convergence applies on balls
([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F4] **Conservation theorem.** For a declared isolated system with energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and flow $U(t)$, a self-adjoint $A$ with
$e^{-isA/\hbar}U(t)=U(t)e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for all $s,t$ has a time-independent
outcome law, conserved moments for vectors in $D(A)$, and a unitary symmetry
$S$ of the dynamics satisfies $SU(t)=U(t)S$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F5] **Outcome laws.** The outcome law of an assigned sharp observable is
$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, respectively
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, with the spectral PVMs of the model's
self-adjoint operators ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clauses (b),(e), [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the symmetry criterion off the conjugation
identity for the bounded-potential operator, prove that a potential invariant
under every translation is almost everywhere constant by mollification and
Lebesgue-point convergence, and instantiate the conservation theorem for the
momentum components of an invariant model.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Symmetry criterion] The identity $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$ is [F1], and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry exactly when $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V}$ with $T_{a}D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}$, which by the identity holds exactly when $H_{V_{a}}=H_{V}$. Subtracting the common free part $H_{0}$ (self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}$ by [F2]) gives $M_{V_{a}}=M_{V}$ as bounded operators, and by [F2] this is equivalent to $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere. This proves (a). [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 [Invariance makes the mollifications constant] Assume $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $x,a\in\mathbb R^{3}$. By [F3] the function $y\mapsto V(y)\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-a-y)$ is integrable, and the substitution $z=y-a$ together with the translation invariance of Lebesgue measure gives $(V*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x-a)=\int V(y)\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-a-y)\,dy=\int V(z+a)\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-z)\,dz$. Since $V(z+a)=V(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-z)$ is a bounded measurable weight, dominated convergence over the ball of radius $\varepsilon$ gives $\int(V(z+a)-V(z))\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-z)\,dz=0$, so $(V*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x-a)=(V*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x)$ for all $x,a$; being continuous, $V*\rho_{\varepsilon}$ is constant, equal to some $c_{\varepsilon}$. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 [Lebesgue points and constancy] Let $B_{R}\subset\mathbb R^{3}$ and put $f:=V\mathbf 1_{B_{R+1}}\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$, a bounded function of bounded support. By [F3] almost every $x\in B_{R}$ is a Lebesgue point of $f$, and for such $x$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$ the mollification of $f$ at $x$ coincides with $(V*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x)$ because the support of $\rho_{\varepsilon}(x-\cdot)$ lies in $B_{R+1}$; hence $V(x)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}(V*\rho_{\varepsilon})(x)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}c_{\varepsilon}$ for almost every $x\in B_{R}$, where the last limit exists by step 1.2 and is independent of $x$ in $B_{R}$. Covering $\mathbb R^{3}$ by countably many such balls, the constants agree on the overlaps, so $V$ is almost everywhere constant, with $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ for that constant $c$ by [F2], and the translations are symmetries by (a) and form a strongly continuous unitary group (the group of clauses (c),(d) of [F1]). This proves (b). [step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 [Momentum conservation] Let $V=c$ almost everywhere, so $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$. For fixed $k$, the group $W(s):=e^{-isP_{k}/\hbar}=T_{se_{k}}$ of [F1] consists of unitaries $S$ with $SD(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$ and $SH_{V}S^{*}=H_{V}$: the identity for $P_{k}$ in [F1] gives $T_{se_{k}}P_{k}T_{se_{k}}^{-1}=P_{k}$ and hence the same for $P_{k}^{2}$ and for $H_{V}$ with its domain. By [F4] applied to the unitary symmetry $S=T_{se_{k}}$, $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$, where $U$ is the flow of $H_{V}$; hence the conservation conclusion of [F4] applies with $A:=P_{k}$, giving the displayed time-independence of the momentum law for every preparation and, for $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$, the conservation of the mean and second moment with the time-zero values of [F4] and [F5]. The generator statement is [F1]. This proves (c). [step 2.1, F1, F4, F5, given, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 prove (a)-(c); clause (d) records the bounded measurable class of potentials, the explicit exclusion of momentum conservation for non-invariant potentials, and the absence of discrete-symmetry, singular-potential, apparatus and empirical claims. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where translation invariance fails.** For a nonconstant bounded measurable
  potential there are always translations $a$ with $V_{a}\ne V$ almost
  everywhere, and then $T_{a}$ is not a symmetry; the companion page exhibits
  such a potential. Covariance is not conservation.
- **The role of boundedness.** The proof of the constancy criterion uses only
  boundedness and measurability of $V$; no regularity, decay or periodicity is
  assumed, and no conclusion is drawn for potentials outside this class.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the framework postulates for the componentwise massive model with a real bounded measurable potential V: the translation T_a is a symmetry of the bounded-potential operator H_V exactly when V is invariant under translation by a, the full translation group is a symmetry group exactly when V is almost everywhere constant, and for such translation-invariant models the momentum components are conserved observables by the generator-conservation theorem. The statement concerns real bounded measurable potentials only; it asserts no momentum conservation for non-invariant potentials, no statement about singular or unbounded potentials, no lattice or discrete symmetry claim, no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.1, 4.2 and 4.3, printed pages 59-69 (PDF pages 67-77): translating kets, the momentum as generator of translations, and translational invariance with conservation of momentum

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): the one-parameter unitary group of translations, its generator, and momentum conservation for the free motion; Theorem 8.1 printed page 174 (PDF page 186)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): conserved operators as those commuting with the Hamiltonian

items.title: Rotational and parity invariance of bounded-potential models: symmetries and conservation of angular momentum and parity laws
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$r=2s+1$, be the model's state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$,
let $U(R)$ be the spatial rotation action and $\Pi$ the spatial parity action
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]), let $U_{i}(t)=U(R_{i}(t))$ be the
coordinate rotation subgroups with Stone generators $L_{i}$ on the Schwartz
classes ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]), let
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),\qquad V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x),\quad V_{P}(x):=V(-x),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)).
Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$, and $U(R)$
is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, then every $U(R)$
is a symmetry, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary
symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each generator $L_{i}$ is a
conserved observable of the model with energy $H_{V}$ in the unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]): for every preparation $\rho$,
every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $L_{i}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) if $V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, then $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on
$W^{2,2}$, so $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and $\Pi$ is a symmetry if and
only if $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere; moreover, reading the self-adjoint
unitary $\Pi$ as an assigned sharp observable with its spectral coordinate in
the dimensionless unit of its eigenvalues $\pm1$, the outcome law of $\Pi$ is
time-independent in every preparation:
$$\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the
cited mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. Rotations and parity act on the spatial factor
only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of the internal factor and no spin angular
momentum are introduced. The rotational and parity invariance hypotheses are
exactly the displayed almost-everywhere identities; no concrete potential,
apparatus, measured spectrum or empirical result is asserted, and no
characterization of the invariant potentials beyond these identities is
claimed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space
$H_{s}$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$; the rotation action $U$ and its
coordinate subgroups $U_{i}$ with generators $L_{i}$; the parity action
$\Pi$; a real bounded measurable $V$; the operator $H_{V}$ with flow $U(t)$;
a preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B$; $R\in SO(3)$;
$i\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $t,s\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Model.** $H_{V}$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and generates the strongly
continuous unitary group $U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a), [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).
A symmetry of the declared dynamics with energy $H_{V}$ is a unitary $S$ with
$S\,D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$ and $S\,H_{V}=H_{V}\,S$ on $D(H_{V})$; a unitary
symmetry group is a group of such symmetries; a one-parameter symmetry group
has all its members symmetries and its generator is furnished by Stone's
theorem
([[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clauses
(b)-(d), [[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]],
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

[F2] **Rotation action.** $U(R)$ is unitary, $U(I)=\mathrm{id}$,
$U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$, $R\mapsto U(R)f$ is continuous for every $f$, and
$U(R)\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$,
$U(R)W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$;
moreover $U(R)H_{0}U(R)^{-1}=H_{0}$ for the free operator
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and
$U(R)M_{V}U(R)^{-1}=M_{V_{R}}$, hence
$U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clauses (a)-(c),
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]], [[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]).

[F3] **Multiplier equality.** For real bounded measurable functions
$V_{1},V_{2}$ one has $M_{V_{1}}=M_{V_{2}}$ if and only if
$V_{1}=V_{2}$ almost everywhere
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a), [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F4] **Parity action.** $\Pi$ is unitary, $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Pi^{*}=\Pi$; $\Pi W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$;
$\Pi H_{0}\Pi=H_{0}$ and $\Pi M_{V}\Pi=M_{V_{P}}$, hence
$\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V_{P}}$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]] clauses (a),(d)).

[F5] **Rotation generators.** For each $i$, $t\mapsto U_{i}(t)$ is a strongly
continuous one-parameter unitary group with $U_{i}(t)=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ for
a self-adjoint generator $L_{i}$, and
$L_{i}\psi=-i\hbar\sum_{j}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}D_{j}\psi$ on
$\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clauses
(a),(b), [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]).

[F6] **Conservation theorem.** For a declared isolated system with energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and flow $U(t)$, the following are equivalent: commutation of
the flows $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ of a self-adjoint $A$ with $W(s)=e^{-isA/\hbar}$,
strong spectral commutation of the PVMs, and domain preservation with
$U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$; when they hold the outcome law of $A$ is time-independent
in every preparation and the mean and second moment are conserved for unit
vectors in $D(A)$; a unitary symmetry $S$ satisfies $SU(t)=U(t)S$ for every
$t$; and a self-adjoint unitary symmetry has a time-independent outcome law
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F7] **Outcome laws and moments.** For an assigned sharp observable $A$ one has
$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$ and
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, and for a unit vector
$\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and second moment of the law exist and equal
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b),(e),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the rotation covariance off the rotation
action, convert the symmetry definition into the operator identity and apply
the multiplier criterion, transfer the conservation theorem to the coordinate
rotation generators, and handle parity as the discrete self-adjoint unitary
symmetry.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [Rotation covariance and symmetry criterion] By [F2] one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ and $U(R)D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$; by [F1] the unitary $U(R)$ is a symmetry exactly when also $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V}$ as operators on $W^{2,2}$, that is exactly when $H_{V_{R}}=H_{V}$. Both sides are self-adjoint with the same domain $W^{2,2}$, so subtracting the common free part $H_{0}$ of [F2] gives the equivalent condition $M_{V_{R}}=M_{V}$, which by [F3] is equivalent to $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 [Invariance gives a unitary symmetry group] Assume $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$. By step 1.1 each $U(R)$ is a symmetry; by [F2] the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ satisfies $U(I)=\mathrm{id}$, $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ and strong continuity, so it is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group in the sense of [F1]. [step 1.1, F2, given]

2.2 [Parity symmetry and conserved parity law] Assume $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere. By [F4] $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V_{P}}=H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$ and $\Pi W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, $\Pi$ being unitary and self-adjoint; hence by [F1] $\Pi$ is a symmetry. Conversely, if $\Pi$ is a symmetry, then $H_{V_{P}}=\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$, and subtracting the common free part gives $M_{V_{P}}=M_{V}$, so $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere by [F3]. Reading $\Pi$ as a self-adjoint unitary assigned sharp observable, applying [F6] clause (c) to the unitary symmetry $S:=\Pi$ gives $\Pi U(t)=U(t)\Pi$ for every $t$ and the time-independence of the outcome law of the assigned sharp observable $(\Pi,u)$ in every preparation, which by [F7] is the displayed identity $\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)$; the spectral coordinate of $\Pi$ takes the eigenvalues $\pm1$ in the dimensionless unit. This proves (c). [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, F6, F7, given, algebra]

3.1 [Conservation of the rotation generators] Fix $i$ and $s\in\mathbb R$. Since $R_{i}(s)\in SO(3)$, step 2.1 makes $U_{i}(s)=U(R_{i}(s))$ a symmetry, so by [F6] the first part of clause (c) gives $U_{i}(s)U(t)=U(t)U_{i}(s)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. By [F5], $W(s):=e^{-isL_{i}/\hbar}=U_{i}(s)$; hence the flow-commutation condition (i) of [F6] holds for the self-adjoint generator $L_{i}$ and the flow $U$ of $H_{V}$. Applying [F6] clauses (a),(b) to that pair and reading the laws through [F7] gives the time-independence of $\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ in every preparation and the conservation of the mean and second moment for $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ with the time-zero values $\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$; the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$ is the unit of the spectral coordinate of $L_{i}$ in the model's units of [F5] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This proves (b). [step 2.1, F5, F6, F7, given, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a); step 2.1 proves the symmetry-group assertion and step 3.1 the conservation assertions of (b); step 2.2 proves (c); clause (d) records the spatial-factor-only reading of the actions, the exact almost-everywhere form of the invariance hypotheses and the exclusion of any concrete-potential, spinorial, apparatus or empirical claim. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Invariance is the hypothesis, not a universal property.** A generic bounded
  measurable potential satisfies neither $V_{R}=V$ nor $V_{P}=V$; the
  companion page exhibits a smooth bounded nonconstant potential with no
  translation symmetry, and the same mechanism obstructs generic rotational
  and parity invariance.
- **Discrete parity has no generator.** $\Pi$ is an involution, so its
  conservation is read directly from the commutation with the flow through the
  self-adjoint unitary clause of the conservation theorem; no one-parameter
  group and no Stone generator is attached to it.
items.physical_scope: Conditional symmetry and conservation statements for the massive spin-s model with a real bounded measurable potential: spatial rotations conjugate the bounded-potential energy operator to the rotated potential, rotational invariance makes every rotation a symmetry and the coordinate-rotation generators conserved sharp observables, and parity invariance makes the parity action a symmetry with a time-independent parity outcome law. The item asserts no symmetry of any concrete potential outside the stated invariance hypotheses, no spinorial or internal rotation action, no SU(2) lift, no apparatus and no empirical result.

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): conserved operators as those commuting with the Hamiltonian and their constant Heisenberg representatives

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Sections 1.2-1.3, printed pages 6-11 (PDF pages 6-11): the angular momentum operators and their commutation relations, and the commutativity of the angular momentum operators with any central-potential Hamiltonian (equation (1.70))

items.title: Gauge covariance of the prescribed-coupling model: unitary equivalence, the symmetry criterion and the transported propagator
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the postulates P1, P2 and P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (a),
for a **declared isolated system** whose energy operator is the
prescribed-coupling minimal-coupling operator of
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]]: a declared spinless
particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, with
admissible prescribed potentials $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ and
energy operator $K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ on the domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]).
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
be an open interval and let $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ be a real
gauge function satisfying the two regularity hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation]]
(for every $t$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^{2}$ with bounded first and second
spatial derivatives, uniformly in $t$; and $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is
differentiable with bounded $\partial_{t}\chi$). Put
$$\theta(x,t):=\frac{q}{\hbar}\chi(x,t),\qquad A'_{j}(\cdot,t):=A_{j}+D_{j}\chi(\cdot,t),\qquad \Phi'(\cdot,t):=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t),$$
let $G(t)$ be multiplication by $e^{i\theta(\cdot,t)}$, and put
$K:=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}}$,
$H'(t):=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi'(t)}$ and $U(\tau):=e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}$. Then:

(a) **Gauge conjugation and unitary equivalence.** If $\chi$ does not depend
on $t$, then $G:=G(t)$ is independent of $t$, is unitary with
$G\,W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and
$$G\,K\,G^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}},\qquad e^{-itK_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}/\hbar}=G\,e^{-itK/\hbar}\,G^{-1}\quad(t\in\mathbb R):$$
the two prescribed-coupling models are related by the fixed unitary $G$.

(b) **Symmetry criterion and the global-phase case.** For every $t\in I$ the
operator $G(t)$ is unitary, preserves $W^{2,2}$, and is a symmetry of the
declared dynamics with energy $K$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
**if and only if**
$$K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}},$$
that is, if and only if transporting the vector potential while keeping the
original scalar potential reproduces the original operator. In particular, if
$\chi$ is constant, then $\mathbf A'(t)=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$,
$\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$ and $G(t)=e^{i\theta}I$ for the constant
$\theta=q\chi/\hbar$, so that every $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the declared
dynamics (a global phase). No claim is made in the nonconstant case beyond the
displayed criterion.

(c) **Transported propagator and the time-dependent model.** For the general
gauge function of the statement and every $u_{0}\in W^{2,2}$ and $s\in I$, the
curve
$$u(t):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}u_{0}\qquad(t\in I)$$
lies in $W^{2,2}$, is differentiable into $L^{2}$ on $I$, satisfies
$u(s)=u_{0}$ and $i\hbar\,u'(t)=H'(t)u(t)$ for every $t$, and is the unique
such curve; the two-parameter family $U'(t,s):=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}$ consists of
unitaries mapping $W^{2,2}$ onto $W^{2,2}$, with $U'(t,t)=I$ and
$U'(t,r)U'(r,s)=U'(t,s)$. Moreover
$$H'(t)=G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}-q\,\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t),$$
so the family $G(t)$ relates the autonomous model with energy $K$ to the
transformed model whose generator is $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}-q\partial_{t}\chi$; a
genuinely time-dependent family $G(t)$ is a family of unitaries indexed by
time and is not claimed to be a symmetry of the autonomous dynamics except at
those $t$ where the operator identity of (b) holds.

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the prescribed spinless
minimal-coupling model with admissible bounded-coefficient potentials and the
stated gauge regularity, and is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P5a and the
cited operator analysis. It asserts no Maxwell equation, no source or
back-reaction model, no identification of the two coefficient pairs as
descriptions of one physical situation (that reading is part of P5a), no
statement about singular or unbounded potentials, and no apparatus or
empirical result; the gauge multipliers are unitary transformations between
coefficient classes and are symmetries of the fixed dynamics exactly under the
criterion displayed in (b).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5a in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice; the potentials
$(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$, $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, the interval
$I$ and the gauge function $\chi$; the operators $K$, $H'(t)$, the multipliers
$G(t)$, the flow $U(\tau)$; times $s,t\in I$, $\tau\in\mathbb R$; a vector
$u_{0}\in W^{2,2}$.

[F1] **Declared model.** The declared system's energy operator is $K$, a
self-adjoint operator with domain $D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ that
generates the strongly continuous unitary group $U(\tau)=e^{-i\tau K/\hbar}$
([[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]] clauses (i)-(iii),
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]]
clause (c), [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]);
a symmetry of the declared dynamics is a unitary $S$ with
$S\,D(K)=D(K)$ and $S\,K=K\,S$ on $D(K)$, and a unitary symmetry group is a
group of such symmetries ([[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
clauses (b),(c)).

[F2] **Gauge multipliers and covariance.** For every $t\in I$ the operator
$G(t)$ is unitary with $G(t)W^{k,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{k,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
for $k=1,2$; for every $u\in W^{1,2}$ one has
$\bigl(P_{j}-qA'_{j}(\cdot,t)\bigr)G(t)u=G(t)\bigl(P_{j}-qA_{j}\bigr)u$; and
$t\mapsto G(t)h$ is continuous with
$\frac{d}{dt}G(t)h=\frac{iq}{\hbar}\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t)G(t)h$ for every
$h\in L^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation]]
clauses (a),(c),(d)). In particular
$G(t)\,W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, so
$G(t)D(K)=D(K)$ by [F1].

[F3] **Transported operator and propagator.** With
$A'_{j}(\cdot,t)=A_{j}+D_{j}\chi(\cdot,t)$ and
$\Phi'(\cdot,t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t)$ the pair
$(\mathbf A'(t),\Phi'(t))$ is admissible and $H'(t)=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi'(t)}$
is self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]],
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]); on
$W^{2,2}$ one has the operator identities
$G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ and
$H'(t)=G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}-q\,\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t)$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-transported-propagator]] clause (a));
and for every $u_{0}\in W^{2,2}$ and $s\in I$ the curve
$u(t)=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}u_{0}$ is the unique $W^{2,2}$-valued,
$L^{2}$-differentiable solution of $i\hbar u'(t)=H'(t)u(t)$ with $u(s)=u_{0}$,
while $U'(t,s)=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}$ is unitary, maps $W^{2,2}$ onto $W^{2,2}$
and satisfies the composition law
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-transported-propagator]] clauses
(b),(c)).

[F4] **Conjugation calculus.** For a unitary $W$ and a self-adjoint $K$ the
operator $WKW^{-1}$ with domain $WD(K)$ is self-adjoint, and its flow satisfies
$e^{-itWKW^{-1}/\hbar}=We^{-itK/\hbar}W^{-1}$ for every $t$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]]
clause (a)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the transported operator identity and the
domain preservation off the gauge suppliers, turn the symmetry definition into
the operator equality, obtain the flow identity from the conjugation calculus,
and quote the transported propagator for the general time-dependent case.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Transported operator identity and domain preservation] Fix $t\in I$. By [F2] $G(t)$ is unitary and $G(t)W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, so $G(t)D(K)=D(K)$ by [F1]; and by [F3] $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ as an identity of self-adjoint operators with domain $W^{2,2}$. If $\chi$ does not depend on $t$, then $A'_{j}(\cdot,t)=A_{j}+D_{j}\chi$ is independent of $t$ and $\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$, and $G(t)$ is independent of $t$; hence in that case $GKG^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ with domain $W^{2,2}$. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 [Symmetry criterion] By [F1] the unitary $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the declared dynamics with energy $K$ exactly when $G(t)D(K)=D(K)$ and $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K$ on $D(K)$; the domain condition holds by step 1.1, and the operator identity holds exactly when $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$, again by step 1.1. This is the criterion of (b). If $\chi$ is constant, then $D_{j}\chi=0$ as a weak derivative and $\partial_{t}\chi=0$, so $\mathbf A'(t)=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$, $\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$ and $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$; moreover $G(t)=e^{i\theta}I$ with the constant $\theta=q\chi/\hbar$, so $G(t)$ is unitary and commutes with $K$, hence is a symmetry. [step 1.1, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.2 [Flow identity for static gauges] Let $\chi$ be independent of $t$ and put $G:=G(t)$. By step 1.1, $GKG^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}$; applying the flow identity of [F4] to the unitary $G$ and the self-adjoint $K$ gives $e^{-itGKG^{-1}/\hbar}=Ge^{-itK/\hbar}G^{-1}$, which is the second display of (a). Together with step 1.1 this proves (a). [step 1.1, F4, given, algebra]

3.1 [Transported propagator] The general-time claims are exactly [F3]: the curve $u(t)=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}u_{0}$ is the unique $W^{2,2}$-valued solution of the transformed equation, the family $U'(t,s)$ is unitary with the composition law and preserves $W^{2,2}$, and $H'(t)=G(t)KG(t)^{-1}-q\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t)$ on $W^{2,2}$. By step 2.1 the unitary $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the autonomous dynamics at the times $t$ at which $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$, and no symmetry statement is made outside those times; this is (c). [step 2.1, F3, given]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 2.2 prove (a) and (b), and step 3.1 proves (c); clause (d) records that the statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P5a, that the gauge multipliers are unitary equivalences or symmetries exactly under the displayed operator criterion, and that no field equation, physical identification, apparatus or empirical claim is made. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Gauge transformation is not automatically a symmetry.** A gauge
  transformation replaces the coefficient pair; the multiplier is a symmetry
  of the fixed dynamics only when the transported magnetic operator with the
  original scalar potential coincides with the original operator. Constant
  gauges give the global phase, which is a symmetry; the nonconstant case is
  left to the criterion, and no general classification of the pairs for which
  the criterion holds is attempted here.
- **Two readings distinguished.** The theorem proves the operator identities;
  the further reading that the gauge-related coefficient pairs describe the
  same physical situation is part of the adopted postulate P5a and is not a
  mathematical consequence of the identities proved here.
items.physical_scope: The gauge structure of the prescribed-coupling model P5a for a spinless particle with admissible bounded-coefficient potentials: the conjugation identity transporting the minimal-coupling operator to the gauge-transformed potentials, the exact criterion under which the gauge multiplier is a symmetry of the fixed declared dynamics, the global-phase case, and the unitary equivalence of the transformed time-dependent model carrying the transported propagator. The item is conditional on the postulates and the cited operator analysis; it asserts no Maxwell equation, no physical identification of gauges, no claim about nonconstant gauges beyond the displayed operator criterion, and no apparatus or empirical content.
