items.title: Scope and empirical status of the symmetry and conservation items
items.statement:
## What the page establishes

The items of this page are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics.
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] fixes the
vocabulary: a symmetry of the declared dynamics is a unitary preserving the
energy domain and commuting with the energy operator, a unitary symmetry group
is a group of such symmetries, a conserved sharp observable is one whose
outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, and the translations,
spatial rotations, parity and gauge multipliers are recorded as the model's
candidate actions, not as symmetries.
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]] proves the
equivalence between flow commutation, strong spectral commutation and domain
invariance of a self-adjoint observable;
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-free-flow-multiplier-form]] provide the concrete actions
and their operator identities on the component-valued model.
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] proves the equivalence of the
commutation conditions with the conservation of the outcome law and the
conservation of moments, and covers self-adjoint unitary symmetries;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
decides exactly which bounded potentials have the translations as symmetries
and derives momentum conservation for the translation-invariant case;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] does the same for
rotations (with conservation of the coordinate-rotation generators) and for
parity; and [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-gauge-covariance]] transports the
prescribed-coupling operator under gauge transformations of
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]], exhibits the exact
criterion under which a gauge multiplier is a symmetry of the fixed dynamics
and identifies the global-phase case. Every one of these statements is
conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P5a and P6 in their stated readings, on the
choice assumptions displayed with the items, and on the cited operator
analysis.

## Empirical status of the symmetry and conservation statements

The conservation laws proved here are model consequences: they hold for the
declared massive model with the displayed potential class and follow from the
invariance hypotheses as identities about that model. They are not reports of
measurements and do not establish that any laboratory preparation is exactly
described by the model. In particular, the mass parameter $m>0$, the charge
parameter $q$, the spin label $s$ and the potentials $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$
are declared model data in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the statement that a concrete
species, field configuration or apparatus realizes them is a tested
identification with uncertainty, external to these items. A selection rule or
a conservation law deduced here becomes an empirical prediction only after a
preparation map, a detection model, a sampling model and an uncertainty
budget are supplied, none of which this page provides. The agreement of such
an identified model with data is evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; it is not a proof of the postulates.

## What is not claimed

The page asserts no symmetry of any concrete potential outside the displayed
almost-everywhere invariance hypotheses, no classification of centrally
symmetric or parity-even systems beyond those hypotheses, no definite value
of a conserved observable, and no converse from the constancy of outcome laws
to the commutation conditions for unbounded observables. The rotation and
parity actions act on the spatial factor only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of
the internal factor and no spin angular momentum appear here; antiunitary and
time-reversal symmetries, superselection sectors, gauge freedom beyond the
prescribed bounded-coefficient class, singular or unbounded potentials,
confined and boundary realizations, periodic potentials, time-dependent
external fields, relativistic matter and full field theory are all outside
the scope of these items and require their own model assumptions.

## Recorded supplier note

The gauge items of this page consume the magnetic-operator development of an
earlier batch of this run. A scoped physics-content check over this page's
dependency closure currently reports no error naming any consumed supplier:
the role metadata of the consumed magnetic-operator items was repaired upstream
after an earlier batch reported it, and the statements and complete proofs
consumed here were inspected in their current form. Separately, the batch notes
of this page record that two consumed supplier items still cite a Teschl
section that does not exist in the author-hosted full text named by their URL
(the citation locators `Section 7.8 pp. 168-171` in
`def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator`,
`thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation` and
`thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-transported-propagator`); the
mathematical content of those items is proved locally by their own complete
arguments, which is what this page consumes, and the citation repair belongs to
their owning batch.

items.title: Definite parity of nondegenerate eigenstates and the position-matrix-element selection rule
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ and the parity action $\Pi$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]); assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded
and measurable with
$$V(-x)=V(x)\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
let
$$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
and put $V_{P}(x):=V(-x)$. Then:

(a) if $\psi\in D(H_{V})$ is an eigenvector of $H_{V}$ with eigenvalue
$E\in\mathbb R$, $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$ and $\psi\ne0$, then $\Pi\psi$ is again an
eigenvector of $H_{V}$ with the same eigenvalue $E$; consequently every
eigenspace of $H_{V}$ is invariant under $\Pi$;

(b) if the eigenspace of $E$ is one-dimensional, then $\Pi\psi=\lambda\psi$
with $\lambda\in\{-1,1\}$: the state has definite parity;

(c) if $\psi,\psi'\in H_{s}$ are unit vectors with $\Pi\psi=\sigma\psi$ and
$\Pi\psi'=\tau\psi'$ for signs $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}$ and $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$,
then
$$\sigma=\tau\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=0;$$
the position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes, while no
nonvanishing statement is made for opposite parities;

(d) **Scope.** The example is conditional on the postulates and the cited
mathematics; the matrix element of (c) is an identity about the model's
assigned position observables. No transition rate, no spectral intensity, no
time-dependent coupling, no measurement model and no empirical consequence is
computed; the hypothesis that the relevant eigenvalue is nondegenerate is
essential for (b).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice; the state space $H_{s}$; the
operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$; the parity action $\Pi$; a real bounded measurable
$V$ with $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere; the operator $H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$; an
eigenvector $\psi$ with eigenvalue $E$; unit vectors $\psi,\psi'$ with
parities $\sigma,\tau$; a coordinate $j$.

[F1] **Model and evenness.** $H_{V}$ is self-adjoint with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a)); under the hypothesis $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere the parity
theorem gives $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$ and
$\Pi W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] clause (c),
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]).

[F2] **Parity action.** $\Pi$ is unitary, $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Pi^{*}=\Pi$; and $\Pi D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ with $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$ as an
identity of operators with domain $D(Q_{j})$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Inner-product calculus.** $H_{s}$ is a complex inner-product space
with sesquilinear pairing, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear
in the second ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]); for a
self-adjoint operator $T$ and vectors $u\in D(T)$, $v\in H$ one has
$\langle Tu,v\rangle=\langle u,Tv\rangle$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; conjugate the eigenvalue equation by the
involution $\Pi$, use one-dimensionality for definite parity, and evaluate
the position matrix element through the operator identity $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$
and the self-adjointness of $\Pi$.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Eigenspaces are parity invariant] By [F1] one has $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$; multiplying this identity on the left by $\Pi=\Pi^{-1}$ gives $H_{V}\Pi=\Pi H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$, again using $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ of [F2]. For an eigenvector $\psi\in D(H_{V})$ the vector $\Pi\psi$ lies in $D(H_{V})$ because $\Pi W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, and $H_{V}(\Pi\psi)=\Pi H_{V}\psi=\Pi(E\psi)=E\,\Pi\psi$; since $\Pi$ is injective, $\Pi\psi\ne0$ whenever $\psi\ne0$. Hence $\Pi$ maps every eigenspace into itself, which is (a). [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 [Definite parity in the nondegenerate case] If the eigenspace of $E$ is one-dimensional and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector, then $\Pi\psi$ belongs to that eigenspace by step 1.1, so $\Pi\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. Applying $\Pi$ again and using $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ gives $\psi=\Pi^{2}\psi=\lambda\,\Pi\psi=\lambda^{2}\psi$; since $\psi\ne0$, $\lambda^{2}=1$ and hence $\lambda\in\{-1,1\}$. This proves (b). [step 1.1, F2, given, algebra]

3.1 [Selection rule] By [F2] the identity $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$ holds with domain $D(Q_{j})$ preserved; multiplying on the left and on the right by $\Pi$ gives $Q_{j}=-\Pi Q_{j}\Pi$ as an identity with domain $D(Q_{j})$. Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$. Then $\Pi\psi\in D(Q_{j})$ by [F2], so $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi\psi$ is defined, and by the operator identity and $\Pi\psi=\sigma\psi$ one has $Q_{j}\psi=-\Pi Q_{j}\Pi\psi=-\sigma\,\Pi Q_{j}\psi$. Since $\Pi^{*}=\Pi$ by [F2] and $\Pi\psi'=\tau\psi'$, taking the pairing with $\psi'$ gives $\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\langle\Pi Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\langle Q_{j}\psi,\Pi\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\tau\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle$ by [F3]. Hence $(1+\sigma\tau)\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=0$, and if $\sigma=\tau$ then $\sigma\tau=1$ and the matrix element vanishes. This proves (c). [step 2.1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), and step 3.1 proves (c); clause (d) records that only the model's operators and its even-potential hypothesis are used, that the nondegeneracy hypothesis is essential in (b), and that no transition rate, measurement model or empirical claim is made. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the same-parity case vanishes.** The parity action conjugates the
  position operator to its negative, so a matrix element between two states of
  equal parity equals its own negative; the argument uses the involution
  structure and self-adjointness of $\Pi$, not the details of the potential
  beyond its evenness.
- **What a selection rule is not.** The vanishing statement is an identity for
  the model's assigned position observables in the declared even-potential
  model. Turning it into a statement about observed transition intensities
  requires a time-dependent coupling model, the corresponding transition-rate
  analysis, a detection model and a sampling model, none of which is supplied
  here.
items.physical_scope: A model computation for the massive spin-s model with an even real bounded measurable potential: the parity invariance of every energy eigenspace, the definite parity of nondegenerate eigenstates, and the vanishing of the position matrix element between two states of the same parity. The item is a conditional identity about the model's operators and assigned position observables; it computes no transition rate, models no measurement and records no empirical result.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.4 and 4.2, printed pages 62-67 (PDF pages 70-75): the parity operator and its eigenvalues, the commutation of parity with the Hamiltonian for an even potential (equation (4.43)) and the vanishing of matrix elements of a vector operator between states of equal definite parity (equation (4.42), printed page 67); PDF page = printed page + 8

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 2.2-2.3.1, printed pages 39-47 (PDF pages 42-50): parity of energy eigenfunctions for even potentials (printed page 39) and the even and odd bound-state solutions of the finite potential well; PDF page = printed page + 3

items.title: The free model: translation symmetries and conserved momentum in the momentum representation
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c));
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Consider the **free model**, the bounded-potential
model with $V\equiv0$:
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]]) and
$f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$. Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the translation $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of
$H_{0}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b),
and
$$T_{a}\,e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,T_{a}^{-1}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(a\in\mathbb R^{3},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) in the momentum representation the two actions are the multipliers
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},\qquad U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}},$$
which commute; consequently $T_{a}U(t)=U(t)T_{a}$ for all $a,t$;

(c) **Momentum conservation.** For every $k$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is
a conserved observable of the free model: for every preparation $\rho$, Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; the coordinate
translations satisfy $T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$, so the momentum
components are the generators of the translational symmetry groups;

(d) the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time:
$$\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|=\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|\qquad\text{for almost every }p\ \text{and every }\psi\in H_{s};$$
consequently the squared modulus of the momentum representative is the same
almost-everywhere function of $p$ at every time;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the free model $V\equiv0$ only. For a
nonconstant bounded potential the translations need not be symmetries and
momentum need not be conserved; that failure is exhibited on this page. No
trajectory in space, no classical limit, no measurement model and no empirical
result is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space
$H_{s}$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$; the free
operator $H_{0}$ with flow $U(t)$; the momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$; a
preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B$; $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$, $t\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Free operator.** $H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ is self-adjoint and generates the
strongly continuous unitary group $U(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (b),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a), [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]).

[F2] **Translations.** $T_{a}$ is unitary, $T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$,
$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$,
$T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, $T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, and
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (c),(d)).
For a real bounded measurable $V$ with $V_{a}(x)=V(x-a)$ one has
$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$, and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ if and
only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere; if $V$ is almost everywhere constant,
the momentum components are conserved with the law and moment statements of
(c) ([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Momentum representation.** $U^{(r)}$ is unitary, maps
$\mathcal S^{(r)}$ onto itself, satisfies $U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)}$ on
the momentum domains, and conjugates the translations to multipliers:
$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clauses (b),(d)).

[F4] **Free flow as a multiplier.** $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}}$
with $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$ and
$|(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi)(p)|=|(U^{(r)}\psi)(p)|$ for almost every $p$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-free-flow-multiplier-form]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F5] **Bounded multipliers commute.** For bounded measurable $g,h$ on
$\mathbb R^{3}$ the pointwise multiplication operators on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ satisfy $M_{g}M_{h}=M_{gh}$ and
$\|M_{g}\|\le\sup|g|$, and the real case is the multiplication convention of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a); the complex case follows from the same pointwise definition
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]). In particular the unimodular multipliers
$M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$ and $M_{f_{t}}$ are unitary and commute with each
other, since $e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}f_{t}(p)=f_{t}(p)e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$ for
every $p$.

[F6] **Laws.** The outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ is
$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, respectively
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the translation-invariance theorem at the
constant potential $V\equiv0$, express both the translations and the free flow
as bounded multipliers in the momentum representation, and read the modulus
invariance off the free-flow multiplier.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Free symmetries] Apply [F2] with $V\equiv0$, which is real, bounded, measurable and constant almost everywhere: $T_{a}H_{0}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{0}$ because $V_{a}\equiv0=V$, so every $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{0}$, and the momentum components are conserved with the law and moment statements displayed in (c). This proves the symmetry assertion of (a) and the conservation clause (c). [F1, F2, F6, given, algebra]

1.2 [Multiplier commutation and explicit conjugation] By [F3] and [F4], conjugating $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}$ by the unitary $U^{(r)}$ gives $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}M_{f_{t}}M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$; by [F5] the multipliers commute and are unitary, with $M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}^{-1}$, so this product equals $M_{f_{t}}$, which is $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}$. Hence $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, which is the second display of (a) and, equivalently, $T_{a}U(t)=U(t)T_{a}$ for all $a,t$: the first display of (b). [F3, F4, F5, given, algebra]

1.3 [Momentum density invariance] The modulus identity of (d) is [F4], and squaring it gives the almost-everywhere invariance of $|(U^{(r)}\psi)(p)|^{2}$ in time; this is the consequence asserted in (d). [F4, given, algebra]

2.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 prove (a), (b), (c) and (d); clause (e) records that the free potential $V\equiv0$ is the only potential used, that no trajectory or measurement model is introduced, and that the failure of translation symmetry for nonconstant potentials is treated separately. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Momentum conservation is translation invariance.** The conservation of
  $P_{k}$ in (c) is the special case $V\equiv0$ of the translation-invariance
  theorem; the point of the example is the explicit multiplier form: both the
  translations and the free flow act in the momentum representation by
  unimodular multipliers, and multipliers of the same variable commute.
- **No trajectory.** The invariance of $|U^{(r)}\psi|$ in the momentum
  variable is a statement about the momentum representative's class, not a
  statement that the particle moves along a classical straight line; no
  position-space trajectory is asserted.
items.physical_scope: A model computation for the free massive spin-s model, V identically zero: the translations are symmetries and commute with the free flow, the momentum components are conserved sharp observables with conserved law and moments, and the free flow acts in the momentum representation as a unimodular multiplier leaving the modulus of the momentum representative fixed. The item asserts nothing for nonconstant potentials, no trajectory, no measured distribution, and no apparatus model.

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): the free evolution as a Fourier multiplier and momentum conservation

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.2, printed pages 20-22 (PDF pages 20-22): constant Heisenberg operators for observables commuting with the Hamiltonian

items.title: A bounded nonconstant potential with no nontrivial translational symmetry
items.statement:
## Statement refuted

Let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be any real, bounded, measurable, nonconstant
function. Then for every nonzero $a\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ the
translation $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of the declared bounded-potential dynamics
with energy $H_{V}$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] and the
postulate items of those readings; the Axioms of Countable Choice and of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the declared
particle of mass $m>0$ and spin label $s$ with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, and translations $T_{a}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c)); the
potential $V_{0}:=1_{B(0,1)}$ and its shift
$V_{0,a}(x):=V_{0}(x-a)$; a vector $a\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$.

[F1] **Model.** For a real bounded measurable $V$ the operator
$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of
$H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere, where $V_{a}(x)=V(x-a)$; in fact
$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
clause (a)).

[F2] **The indicator potential.** $B(0,1)=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|<1\}$ is the
Euclidean unit ball ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]);
$V_{0}=1_{B(0,1)}$ is real, measurable with $0\le V_{0}\le1$, and nonconstant
since $V_{0}(0)=1$ and $V_{0}(2e_{1})=0$. For every $x$,
$$V_{0,a}(x)=1\iff x-a\in B(0,1)\iff |x-a|<1,$$
so $\{x:V_{0}(x)\ne V_{0,a}(x)\}=\{x:|x|<1\le|x-a|\}\cup\{x:|x-a|<1\le|x|\}$.

[F3] **Norm geometry.** The Euclidean norm satisfies the triangle inequality
$|y-a|\ge|x-a|-|y-x|$ and $|y|\le|x|+|y-x|$ for all $x,y,a\in\mathbb R^{3}$
([[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]] clause 1,
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F4] **Lebesgue measure.** A Euclidean ball $B(x,r)$ with $r>0$ is Lebesgue
measurable with $0<\lambda(B(x,r))<\infty$
([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]); Lebesgue
measure is the restriction of Lebesgue outer measure to the measurable sets,
and $\lambda^{*}$ is monotone
([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]],
[[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-is-an-outer-measure-agreeing-with-volume]],
[[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); a property holds almost
everywhere exactly when its exceptional set is contained in a measurable set
of measure zero ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]).

## Counterexample

**Proof technique:** direct; take the indicator of the unit ball, exhibit a
point where the shifted potential differs, show that a whole ball lies in the
difference set, and use the positivity of Lebesgue measure of balls to
conclude that the potentials are not equal almost everywhere, so that the
symmetry criterion fails.

**Given:** The data of the refuted statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [A point where the shifted potential differs] Put $u:=a/|a|$, a unit vector, and $\delta:=\min\{|a|/2,1/2\}>0$, and set $x_{0}:=-(1-\delta)u$. Then $|x_{0}|=1-\delta<1$, so $V_{0}(x_{0})=1$; and $x_{0}-a=-(1-\delta+|a|)u$, so $|x_{0}-a|=1-\delta+|a|>1$ because $|a|>\delta$ for $\delta\le|a|/2$, whence $V_{0,a}(x_{0})=0$. Thus $x_{0}$ lies in the difference set $\{V_{0}\ne V_{0,a}\}$ of [F2]. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 [A ball inside the difference set] Let $y\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with $|y-x_{0}|<\delta/2$ and put $r:=\delta/2$. Then $|y|\le|x_{0}|+|y-x_{0}|<1-\delta+\delta/2<1$, so $V_{0}(y)=1$; and $|y-a|\ge|x_{0}-a|-|y-x_{0}|>1-\delta+|a|-\delta/2=1+|a|-3\delta/2>1$, the last inequality because $\delta\le|a|/2$ gives $3\delta/2\le3|a|/4<|a|$ and, when $\delta=1/2\le|a|$, $3\delta/2=3/4<1\le|a|$; hence $V_{0,a}(y)=0$. Therefore $B(x_{0},r)\subseteq\{V_{0}\ne V_{0,a}\}$. [step 1.1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 [The difference set has positive measure] By [F4] the ball $B(x_{0},r)$ is measurable with $\lambda(B(x_{0},r))>0$. If $V_{0,a}=V_{0}$ almost everywhere, then the difference set $\{V_{0}\ne V_{0,a}\}$ is contained in a measurable null set $N$, and step 2.1 gives $B(x_{0},r)\subseteq N$; monotonicity of the outer measure [F4] then yields $\lambda(B(x_{0},r))=\lambda^{*}(B(x_{0},r))\le\lambda^{*}(N)=\lambda(N)=0$, contradicting $\lambda(B(x_{0},r))>0$. Hence $V_{0,a}\ne V_{0}$ almost everywhere. [step 2.1, F4, given, algebra]

4.1 [The refutation] By step 3.1 and the symmetry criterion of [F1], $T_{a}$ is not a symmetry of $H_{V_{0}}$ for the displayed nonzero $a$. Since $a\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ was arbitrary and $V_{0}$ is real, bounded, measurable and nonconstant by [F2], the universally quantified statement is refuted: a bounded nonconstant potential need not have any nontrivial translational symmetry. [step 3.1, F1, F2, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the failure comes from.** The criterion [F1] is an almost-everywhere
  identity of the shifted potential classes, and the example realizes the
  failure on a set of positive measure. Boundedness and measurability suffice
  for the model to be well posed; they do not produce any translation
  symmetry.
- **What is not claimed.** The counterexample refutes one universal statement
  about bounded nonconstant potentials; it does not claim that every bounded
  nonconstant potential has no nontrivial translational symmetry (potentials
  constant along a direction do have the corresponding translations as
  symmetries), and it makes no statement about any laboratory potential or
  measurement.
items.physical_scope: A counterexample inside the declared massive model with a bounded measurable potential: the indicator of the unit ball has no nontrivial translational symmetry, so no nonzero translation commutes with its bounded-potential energy operator, while the potential itself is bounded and measurable and its model is self-adjoint on W^{2,2}. The item refutes a universal claim about translations of bounded nonconstant potentials; it asserts nothing about the physics of a laboratory potential and records no measurement.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.3, printed pages 68-70 (PDF pages 76-78): translational invariance of a potential as the condition for momentum conservation
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): momentum conservation for potentials invariant under translations

items.title: A radial bounded potential: rotational and parity symmetry and conservation of the rotation generators
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$, rotation action $U(R)$ and coordinate-rotation generators
$L_{i}$ ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]); assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $v:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and
measurable, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and
measurable with
$$V(x)=v(|x|)\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb R^{3},$$
a **radial potential almost everywhere** (if $V$ is the composition
$x\mapsto v(|x|)$ everywhere, this holds with empty exceptional set). Let
$$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the bounded-potential energy operator. Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $V(R^{-1}x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, and
$V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$;

(b) every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a
strongly continuous unitary symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved observable: for every preparation $\rho$,
Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
with conserved mean and second moment for unit vectors in $D(L_{i})$ and
time-zero values $\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$, $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$, in the
unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]);

(c) the parity action $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and its outcome law in
every preparation is time-independent;

(d) **Scope.** The example is conditional on the postulates and the bounded
radial class; it computes no eigenvalue, no bound state, no degeneracy and no
radial solution, and the boundedness of $v$ excludes the Coulomb potential and
other unbounded radial models, which require their own self-adjointness and
spectral analysis. No claim is made that any particular physical potential is
radial, and no empirical result is recorded.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space
$H_{s}$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$; the rotation action $U$ and generators
$L_{i}$; a bounded measurable $v$ and a real bounded measurable $V$ with
$V=v(|\cdot|)$ almost everywhere; the operator $H_{V}$; a preparation $\rho$;
a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B$; $R\in SO(3)$; $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ and
$t\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Model reading.** $H_{V}$ is self-adjoint with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$; the rotation action $U(R)$ is unitary
with $U(R)W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$ and strongly continuous in $R$; the coordinate
subgroups $U_{i}(t)=U(R_{i}(t))$ have self-adjoint Stone generators $L_{i}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clauses
(a),(b), [[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]).

[F2] **Orthogonality.** For $R\in SO(3)$ one has $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and
$R^{\mathsf T}=R^{-1}$
([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]], [[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]); the
Euclidean inner product satisfies
$\langle Rx,Rx\rangle=\langle x,R^{\mathsf T}Rx\rangle=\langle x,x\rangle$ and
$|x|^{2}=\langle x,x\rangle$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[F3] **Almost everywhere and orthogonal images.** A property holds almost
everywhere when its exceptional set is contained in a measurable null set
([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); finite unions of null sets
are null, since Lebesgue measure is a measure
([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For an invertible linear
$T$ and measurable $E$ the image $T[E]$ is measurable with
$\lambda(T[E])=|\det T|\,\lambda(E)$; in particular for $R\in SO(3)$ one has
$\det R=1$ and $\lambda(R[E])=\lambda(E)$, so orthogonal images of null sets
are null ([[thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure]] clause 1,
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]).

[F4] **Invariance theorem.** If $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every
$R\in SO(3)$, then every $U(R)$ is a symmetry, $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly
continuous unitary symmetry group, and each $L_{i}$ is conserved with the law
and moment statements displayed in (b); if additionally $V_{P}=V$ almost
everywhere, then $\Pi$ is a symmetry and its outcome law is time-independent
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F5] **Outcome laws.** For an assigned sharp observable $A$ one has
$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; verify the almost-everywhere rotational and
parity invariance of the radial class from orthogonality of the rotation
matrices, and instantiate the rotational-and-parity invariance theorem.

**Given:** The data of the example and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Almost-everywhere rotational invariance] Let $N$ be a measurable null set with $V(x)=v(|x|)$ for every $x\notin N$. Fix $R\in SO(3)$ and let $x\notin N\cup R[N]$. By [F2], $|R^{-1}x|^{2}=\langle R^{-1}x,R^{-1}x\rangle=\langle x,(R^{-1})^{\mathsf T}R^{-1}x\rangle=\langle x,x\rangle=|x|^{2}$, using $(R^{-1})^{\mathsf T}=(R^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=R$, so $|R^{-1}x|=|x|$ and $R^{-1}x\notin N$; hence $V(R^{-1}x)=v(|R^{-1}x|)=v(|x|)=V(x)$. By [F3] the set $R[N]$ is null, so the exceptional set of the identity $V(R^{-1}x)=V(x)$ is null; therefore $V(R^{-1}x)=V(x)$ almost everywhere. For parity, let $x\notin N\cup(-N)$; then $-x\notin N$ and $V(-x)=v(|-x|)=v(|x|)=V(x)$ because $|-x|=|x|$, and $N\cup(-N)$ is null by [F3], so $V(-x)=V(x)$ almost everywhere. This proves (a). [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 [Instantiation] By step 1.1 the hypotheses $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$ and $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere of [F4] hold; applying [F4] gives that every $U(R)$ is a symmetry, that $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group, that each $L_{i}$ is conserved with the displayed law and moment statements read through [F5], and that $\Pi$ is a symmetry with a time-independent outcome law. This proves (b) and (c). [step 1.1, F4, F5, given]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a)-(c) from the model reading [F1]; clause (d) records the bounded radial class, the exclusion of Coulomb and other unbounded radial models and the absence of eigenvalue, bound-state, apparatus and empirical claims. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **What makes the example work.** Only two ingredients are used: the radial
  identity $V(x)=v(|x|)$ almost everywhere and the orthogonality of rotations
  through $|R^{-1}x|=|x|$; the boundedness of $v$ keeps the model inside the
  bounded-potential class of the page, whose self-adjointness and conservation
  results are already established.
- **What an angular-momentum conservation law is here.** The conserved object
  is the outcome law of the assigned generator observable $L_{i}$ (with its
  moments where they exist); no classical angular-momentum vector, no definite
  value and no measured spectral line is asserted.
items.physical_scope: A model example for the massive spin-s model with a bounded measurable potential that is radial almost everywhere: every spatial rotation is a symmetry, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group, the coordinate-rotation generators are conserved sharp observables in J s, and the parity action is a symmetry with a conserved parity law. The item is conditional on the bounded radial class; it asserts no eigenvalue, bound-state or degeneracy claim, no Coulomb or other unbounded radial model, and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 4.1.3-4.3, printed pages 62-70 (PDF pages 70-78): the rotation operator and its generators, the commutator [J_i, S]=0 for scalar operators and the conservation laws of symmetric Hamiltonians; PDF page = printed page + 8

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 4.1.1, printed pages 96-99 (PDF pages 99-102): the angular momentum commutation relations, with the angular momentum operators as the generators of rotations

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', Section 1.3, printed pages 9-11 (PDF pages 9-11): central potentials and the commutativity of the angular momentum operators with the Hamiltonian (equation (1.70))

items.title: What the worked items of the symmetry companion page establish
items.statement:
## The worked items and what they establish

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
this fails as soon as the potential is nonconstant in the relevant direction:
for the bounded measurable indicator potential $1_{B(0,1)}$ no nonzero
translation is a symmetry, because the shifted potential differs from the
original on a set of positive measure, so the symmetry criterion of the
translation theorem is not met.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-central-potential-rotation-invariance]] verifies the
almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

## What none of the items establishes

None of the four items is an experiment: no apparatus, preparation map,
calibration, detection model, efficiency, resolution, background model,
sampling model, uncertainty budget, count or dataset appears, and no measured
value of any model parameter is asserted. The objects $m$, $q$ when present,
$s$, the potentials and the conserved laws are model data and model statements
in the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; deciding that a
laboratory system realizes the model, that its potential is approximately
radial or even, or that a transition amplitude is the matrix element computed
here, is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus assumptions, and it is external to this page. In particular the
parity selection rule is an identity about the model's assigned position
observables: turning it into a statement about observed intensities requires a
time-dependent coupling model, the corresponding transition-rate analysis, a
detection model and a sampling model, none of which is supplied here.

## Limits of the statements

The free computation is conditional on $V\equiv0$; the counterexample concerns
one potential inside the bounded measurable class and refutes only the
universal claim that every bounded nonconstant potential has all nonzero
translations as symmetries (potentials constant along a direction keep the
corresponding translations). The central-potential example assumes the radial
identity almost everywhere and a bounded radial function; it asserts no
eigenvalue, bound state, degeneracy, radial solution or spectral line, and its
boundedness hypothesis excludes the Coulomb and other unbounded radial
models. The parity example requires the evenness hypothesis and, for definite
parity, the nondegeneracy of the eigenvalue; at a degenerate eigenvalue only
the eigenspace invariance is asserted. No item of this page makes a claim about
antiunitary or time-reversal symmetries, about superselection, about spinorial
rotations or the internal factor, or about relativistic and field-theoretic
structures.
